# Activation Clause

Combines a document’s party roster, acceptance boundary, optional terms negotiation and access guard. Hosted bootstrap resolves account locators into authenticated transports before initialization. State and paths belong to the document where this clause executes. Executable hooks come from its admitted exact type.

## Configuration

The clause’s `parameters` configure:

- `parties`: required, nonempty object keyed by party role. Each party needs `lead/channel`; party keys and keys in optional `representatives` must pass the inherited name validator. Its precise naming rules are not supplied.
- `required`: roles whose acceptance is needed; defaults to all initial party keys. An explicitly empty list requires no individual approvals, but cannot enable negotiation.
- `accessPaths`: embedded access-document paths, default `[]`. Their `Timeline Access Updated` events trigger activation refresh. `/partyAccess` is also an embedded collection.
- `readers`: reader configuration passed to access checks, default `{}`. Party `readerKeys` also participate in the access configuration. The detailed permission-matching rules are inherited and not supplied.
- `allowNewParties`: defaults to `false`; controls additions through `updateParty_<role>`.
- `frozen`: defaults to `false`; initial roster state is also frozen when `/partyRosterFrozen` is `true`. Frozen state blocks party updates and approved admissions.
- `revision`: initial activation revision, default `1`.
- `preActivationOperations` and `preActivationChannels`: default `[]`; permit specified deliveries before business readiness, subject to the access and closure checks below.
- `negotiation/allowedPaths`: defaults to `[]`; a nonempty list enables negotiation for `required` roles and requires the executing document to have `/type`.
- `admission/approvers`: a nonempty list is required by the separate approved-admission function. The admission approval procedure itself is not supplied.

Negotiable paths must be unique absolute paths with no empty components or `~`. Their first component cannot be `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name` or `description`. They cannot equal or descend from an `accessPaths` entry. Each selected field must exist and be text, integer, double or Boolean.

## State and acceptance

`/activation` holds the roster, required roles, approvals, access readiness and activation status. Initialization starts `approved` and `accessRequests` as empty objects. Configuration defaults do not establish values for absent runtime state.

- `accessReady` and `functional` record the same access-check result. The check includes the current roster and parties from access requests whose `expectedRevision` matches the current `revision`; pending admission can therefore affect readiness before admission completes.
- `termsAccepted` requires approval for every `required` role and a successful inherited `termsCurrent` check. During this calculation, a missing role approval counts as unapproved. The detailed terms-current test is not supplied.
- `active` requires access readiness, terms acceptance and absence of a true `closed` flag. `everActivated` permanently records whether committed state has ever become active.
- `status` is `CLOSED` when closed; otherwise `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` before first activation or `SUSPENDED_ACCESS` afterward when access is unavailable; otherwise `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` or `ACTIVE`. `reason` reports `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` or an empty string; it does not separately explain closure.

`Clauses Initialized` triggers refresh. Refresh initializes terms when absent, commits computed activation state and updates pending access-request readiness. Initial party transports remain empty composite channels until access is ready; conflicting contract names are rejected.

`/activation/terms/fields` maps negotiable paths to their published scalar values. `terms/definition` identifies the fixed initial document content after excluding those values, configured access documents, activation `accessPaths` and `readers`, and party `readerKeys`. `terms/ref` identifies the definition-and-fields combination. `termsRevision` and `negotiation/revision` initialize to `1`; these and `revision` are version counters.

Public operations take input from `call/request`, identify the invoking channel through `call/channel`, and require `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be `true`.

`approve_<role>` accepts for a party lead. It requires the current `revision`, valid participant access and, when negotiation is enabled, the current `termsRef`. Any supplied `termsRef` must match `/activation/terms/ref`. A new approval records `approved[role] = true`, commits state and emits `Terms Accepted` with `party` and `revision`. Repeating an existing approval returns successfully without another acceptance event. One party’s approval does not establish activation.

The first committed transition to active emits `Document Activated`. Losing access from an active state emits `Document Access Suspended`; becoming active after an earlier activation with previously unavailable access emits `Document Access Restored`. These events carry `revision`. Successful acceptance of current terms that makes the document active closes any pending proposal as `SUPERSEDED` and sets `negotiation/editable` to `false`.

## Negotiation

When enabled, the clause creates `proposeChanges_<role>`, `proposeAndActivate_<role>`, `activate_<role>`, `withdrawAcceptance_<role>`, `withdrawProposal_<role>` and `rejectProposal_<role>` for required roles. Every negotiation call checks membership in `/activation/required` as well as exact document review.

`proposeChanges` takes a user-supplied unique `proposalId`, current `baseTermsRef` and nonempty `changes` list. Each change requires `path` and `replacement`. Paths must be allowed and cannot repeat within the request; replacements must retain the current field’s scalar kind, and the resulting document must conform to its `/type`. Unchanged terms, stale references, closed proposal identifiers and invalid candidates are rejected. Replacing a different pending proposal requires `supersedes` to match its identifier; the old proposal is recorded as `SUPERSEDED`.

Recording a proposal stores its `baseTermsRef`, proposed `termsRef`, replacement fields and proposer. It does not publish the proposed values. `proposeAndActivate` then invokes `activate` for that proposal; its name does not guarantee that the document becomes active.

`activate` requires text `termsRef`:

- For current `/activation/terms/ref`, `proposalId` must be omitted. It invokes ordinary approval using the current activation revision.
- For proposed terms, `proposalId` and `termsRef` must match the pending proposal. The stored base reference, allowed field set, resulting document type and terms identity are revalidated. Proposal approval is delegated to the inherited amendment mechanism with the required roles configured as approvers; its precise completion rule is not supplied. Only when that mechanism marks the proposal closed does this function publish its replacements and reference, increment `termsRevision` and `revision`, carry proposal approvals into `approved`, set `negotiation/editable` to `false`, record `APPLIED` and commit activation state.

`withdrawAcceptance` selects current or proposed terms using the same reference rules and records the invoking role’s approval as `false`. Withdrawal for current terms commits activation state; withdrawal for proposed terms updates proposal approvals without closing the proposal.

`withdrawProposal` requires the matching pending `proposalId` and its original proposer. `rejectProposal` permits a required approver to reject that matching proposal. Both clear the pending proposal, mark its identifier closed in `negotiation/history`, and record `WITHDRAWN` or `REJECTED` in `negotiation/outcomes`. A history value of `true` means closed, not necessarily applied.

Once `everActivated` is true, creating proposals, withdrawing acceptance, and withdrawing or rejecting proposals are rejected as `NEGOTIATION_CLOSED`, including during later access suspension.

## Party changes and admission

`updateParty_<role>` accepts `replacement` party data with `lead/channel` and optional `party`. Omitting `party` targets the invoking party. An existing party lead can replace its own party, or add an explicitly named new party when `allowNewParties` is true; it cannot manage another existing party. No revision input is required. Frozen state, invalid names, missing lead channels, invalid resulting access or contract-name conflicts reject the update.

A successful update installs roster contracts, clears approvals, increments `revision`, adds a new role to `required` when adding, commits state and emits `Party Changed`. When initialized terms exist, a changed roster or required-role set also changes the terms identity, increments `termsRevision`, clears pending proposals with outcome `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`, and clears approvals when negotiation is enabled.

`Party Addition Requested` starts access preparation for an approved admission. It carries `parties`, `accessDocuments`, `admissionRef` and `expectedRevision`; stale revisions and already-recorded admission references are ignored. Supplied Timeline Access histories are checked and installed under `/partyAccess`. Missing access for existing parties produces `Party Access Update Requested` events and records requests under `/activation/accessRequests/<admissionRef>`. Each request’s `ready` reflects an access check, not completed admission. These requests grant neither private timeline access nor participant consent or owner authority. `Timeline Access Updated` confirms a completed access operation; current permissions come from the completed access document.

The separate `admitApprovedParties` function requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, a configured admission policy, inherited main-party compatibility checks and valid resulting access. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`. An accepted addition installs contracts, increments `revision`, commits state and emits `Party Changed` with `kind` set to `Participants admitted` and an `admissionRef`. This path preserves `required`; the terms-identity consequences of roster changes still apply. A callable admission function alone does not establish approval authority.

## Delivery guard and configuration changes

The activation dispatch policy permits triggered `activationInitialized` deliveries and embedded deliveries on configured access-control channels or `/activation/registeredAccessChannels` before its other checks. For other deliveries it rejects missing `/activation` as `ACTIVATION_NOT_INITIALIZED`, unavailable or currently invalid access as `DOCUMENT_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE`, and closed state as `DOCUMENT_CLOSED`.

After those checks, configured external `preActivationOperations` and non-external `preActivationChannels` may run. The operation allowance also includes generated approval, party-update and negotiation operations. Remaining deliveries depend on inherited `businessReady`, with `DOCUMENT_NOT_ACTIVE` on rejection; its detailed criteria are not supplied.

Other installed dispatch policies still apply. A denied delivery skips its handlers; external input is consumed and checkpointed rather than deferred or replayed when readiness changes.

Changing this clause through clause reconfiguration is rejected with `USE_ACTIVATION_PARTY_OPERATIONS`. While negotiation is configured and `everActivated` is not true, changes to the clause configuration set are additionally rejected as `NEGOTIATION_POLICY_LOCKED`.
